name: DeXtreme
summary: DeXtreme retrained cube reorientation on an Allegro Hand entirely inside GPU-accelerated Isaac Gym with automatic domain randomization, cutting the compute requirement from a large cluster to a handful of GPUs and open-sourcing the stack. It showed the sim-to-real dexterity result was a general recipe, not a one-off feat of OpenAI-scale engineering.
innovation: End-to-end GPU simulation and training loop that made high-DoF dexterity affordable.
Careful analysis of which randomizations actually matter for transfer.
matters: Democratized sim-to-real dexterity research and validated GPU-parallel simulation as the standard tool.
limits: Still a single narrow task, with reward shaping doing considerable hidden work.
lineage: Dactyl's approach re-implemented on Isaac Gym's massively parallel GPU simulator.
